comment: Pinned refs for the parser-library comparison. 'old' is what JBrowse 2
resolved at v2.4.0 — the release the 2023 Genome Biology paper benchmarked as
'jb2 parallel' and archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.7710472). The versions
come out of that tag's yarn.lock rather than off its package.json ranges,
because a range is not a version: v2.4.0 asks for @gmod/bam ^1.1.15 and ships
1.1.18. 'new' is the current release, which is also what main's ranges resolve
to today. Both sides are cloned from GitHub at these tags and built from
source with the same toolchain, so the measured difference is library code and
not a change of transpiler target or module format.
jbrowse-components at v2.4.0 (78707a2bc3, 2023-02-24) resolved:
@gmod/bam 1.1.18, @gmod/cram 1.7.3, @gmod/bbi 3.0.0,
@gmod/vcf 5.0.10, @gmod/bgzf-filehandle 1.4.5
Until 2026-08-18 the old side was read off jbrowse-components at its last
commit before 2023-08-15 (rev 6fb9daa575) instead — six months past the
paper, and a whole major line off on two of the five libraries: bam 2.0.0
where the paper shipped 1.1.18, bbi 4.0.0 where it shipped 3.0.0. So the
table named the published version and measured a later one, understating the
change by however much those two majors were worth. What this file exists to
answer is how much faster the parsers got since the version people have read
about, so the pin is the archived release rather than a nearby tree.
The 'new' pins are npm latest as of 2026-08-18. main pins @gmod/bam ^8.9.0,
@gmod/cram ^13.3.0, @gmod/bbi ^11.2.1, @gmod/vcf ^7.2.0 and
@gmod/bgzf-filehandle ^6.6.0, and every one of those ranges resolves to the
tag below, so 'new' is both the current release and what a build of main
installs.
vcf-js appears twice, on two different axes. 'vcf-js' is the 2023-vs-current
comparison every other entry makes. 'vcf-js-scan' is a single-release
before/after, v7.1.1 against v7.2.0, isolating the genotype-scan rewrite that
landed in 7.2.0 — a change whose whole effect is inside the per-sample loop
and would otherwise be invisible inside a two-major-version gap.

extraDepsReason: v1.7.3 imports generic-filehandle without declaring it, in either
dependencies or devDependencies. Under npm's flat node_modules it
resolved anyway, hoisted out of a transitive dep; pnpm's strict layout
does not hoist, so the import fails. ^3.0.0 is the range
